source.title: Anterior prefrontal function and the limits of human decision-making

confidence_rationale: Canonical Science account of frontopolar (lateral area 10) cognitive branching: the FPC holds a pending task-set in a counterfactual ('to be re-engaged later') state while another is executed. Directly grounds the SD-046 pending/parked-slot primitive and SD-033e's engage<->deliberate transition. Confidence held below 0.8 because the paper's headline structural finding -- branching is restricted to ONE pending alternative (recursive branching beyond two tasks fails) -- qualifies rather than fully endorses SD-046's N=2-4 range; the mapping from human task-branching to an artificial multi-slot GoalState is an architectural analogy, not a measured isomorphism.
failure_signatures: Koechlin & Hyafil find a STRUCTURAL limit of one pending branch: humans cannot recursively branch between more than two tasks. If SD-046 instantiates N=3-4 hard discrete slots that all maintain full counterfactual branch status simultaneously, this paper predicts that beyond the second pending slot the architecture will not deliver genuine branch-and-return behaviour -- the extra slots would degrade to stored-but-not-branchable goals.

The branching signal is specific to lateral FPC (area 10); if a V4 SD-033e-analog placed counterfactual maintenance in a vmPFC/OFC-analog value module instead, the dissociation Koechlin reports would be lost.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Lateral anterior prefrontal cortex (frontopolar, area 10) implements cognitive branching: it maintains a pending task-set in a counterfactual state for delayed re-engagement while a concurrent task is executed. This capacity is subject to a hard structural limit -- humans can hold one pending branch (two tasks total), not recursive branches beyond that.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-046's multi-slot GoalState is the architectural realisation of branching: a parked goal slot holds an interrupted task's counterfactual ('resume later') status while another slot's trajectory commits, and SD-033e is the frontopolar-analog substrate that hosts the engage<->deliberate transition. The Koechlin limit translates to a prior on the slot count: the honest default for SD-046 is N=2 (one active + one pending branch), with N=3-4 treated as a capacity-bounded extension (see Cowan/Bays&Husain/Heilbronner entries) rather than a free parameter.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human dual-task branching is not the same construct as a maintained set of parallel goal slots; Koechlin's task alternates between TWO task-sets, whereas SD-046 proposes simultaneously-active goals each generating its own ghost-bank rank and proposer trajectories. The paper grounds the PENDING-BRANCH primitive and its limit, not the full parallel-arbitration claim (that is MECH-265's territory).
mapping.source_context: Human model-based fMRI + behaviour; task-switching / branching paradigm; healthy adults.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Science, model-based fMRI, foundational and heavily replicated framing). Mapping_fidelity moderate-high: the pending-branch primitive maps cleanly onto the parked slot, but the structural-2 limit is a constraint on SD-046, not a blanket endorsement. Transfer_risk moderate: human->artificial-agent, and the FPC localisation is human-specific (Mansouri 2017 notes parallel-goal monitoring is human-elaborated).
